```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
x <- params$x
s <- x$settings
tier_table <- gpmapr:::.report_tier_table(x)
links_table <- gpmapr:::.report_links_table(x)
direction_table <- gpmapr:::.report_direction_table(x)
family_table <- gpmapr:::.report_family_table(x)
excluded_table <- gpmapr:::.report_excluded_table(gpmapr::excluded(x))
biology <- gpmapr::annotation(x, "summary")
```

<p class="note">Written by `create_report()` from a `trait_correspondence()`
result (gpmapr `r x$gpmapr_version`, run `r format(x$created, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")`).</p>

Each trait was decomposed independently into SNP programs. Every cross-trait
pair of high- and medium-confidence programs was then asked two questions.
**Same biology?** Are the two programs driven by the same background traits
in the same proportions (`phi_traits`, the Tucker congruence of their trait
loadings)? **Same SNPs?** Where the two traits share fine-mapped loci, do the
programs load on them alike (`alignment`, with a permutation test,
`q_concordance`)? The answers give each pair a tier; high- and medium-tier
pairs are **links**, and links are grouped into multi-trait **families**. The
**direction** of a link (do the alleles raise both traits, or raise one and
lower the other?) is the sign of `phi_traits`, checked against the traits' own
allele effects where enough loci are shared (`rg`).

## Traits compared

```{r results = "asis"}
print(knitr::kable(x$traits, format = "html", caption = "Traits and their programs (high and medium confidence) and loci"))
```

```{r results = "asis"}
if (nrow(excluded_table) > 0) {
  cat(
    "\n\nProxy traits of each anchor, removed from its fit and left out of every ",
    "profile comparison involving it (see each trait's decomposition for how closely ",
    "each tracks its anchor):\n\n", sep = ""
  )
  cat('<details><summary>Proxy traits removed</summary><div class="table-wrap">')
  print(knitr::kable(excluded_table, format = "html"))
  cat("</div></details>\n\n")
}
```

## How many program pairs link

Two traits can only be matched at loci both were fine-mapped to, so
`n_loci_shared` bounds how much locus evidence exists for a pair of traits.

| tier | profile (`phi_traits`) | loci | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| **high** | strong (\|phi\| >= `r s$phi_high`) | agree | same biology, carried by the same SNPs |
| **medium** | strong | too few to check | same biology; too few shared loci to check the SNPs |
| **medium** | moderate (>= `r s$phi_low`) | agree | a weaker profile match, confirmed by the SNPs |
| **low** | strong / moderate / weak | disagree / too few / agree | not a link |

Loci are **too few** with fewer than `r s$min_shared_loci` shared
high-confidence loci or fewer than `r s$min_eff_loci` effective loci; they
**agree** when `alignment` >= `r s$min_alignment` and `q_concordance` <=
`r s$fdr_threshold`.

```{r results = "asis"}
print(knitr::kable(tier_table, format = "html", caption = "Program pairs per trait pair, by tier"))
```

```{r results = "asis"}
if (is.finite(x$q_floor)) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "<p class=\"note\">With n_perm = %d permutations, a locus p-value cannot fall below ",
    "1/%d; after correction across all %d scored pairs, pairs at that floor have ",
    "q = %.3g. If that is close to fdr_threshold (%s), loci cannot agree because there ",
    "are too few permutations: rerun with a larger n_perm.</p>"
  ), as.integer(s$n_perm), as.integer(s$n_perm) + 1L, sum(is.finite(x$pairs$q_concordance)),
  x$q_floor, format(s$fdr_threshold)))
}
```

```{r fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
print(gpmapr::plot_phi(x))
```

## Links

Every pair of tier low or above (green high, orange medium, red low), by tier
and then by |phi|. `top_traits` are the background traits carrying the
profile match, with their share (a negative share works against phi's sign).
`n_eff_traits` is how many traits effectively carry it: a match carried by one
or two traits is a narrower claim. `comparability` is how much of the two
programs the shared loci cover. `rg` (with its 95% interval) is the
correlation of the two traits' own allele effects across the programs' loci;
`direction_check` says whether it agrees with the profile direction.

```{r results = "asis"}
if (nrow(links_table) == 0) {
  cat("No program pair reached the low tier.\n\n")
} else {
  cat('<div class="table-wrap">')
  print(gpmapr::kable_confidence(links_table, tier_col = "tier", caption = "Program pairs of tier low or above"))
  cat("</div>")
}
```

```{r results = "asis"}
if (nrow(direction_table) > 0) {
  print(knitr::kable(
    direction_table, format = "html",
    caption = "Links per trait pair by profile direction, and whether rg (where it calls a direction) agrees"
  ))
}
```

## Families

Links are grouped into families by community detection on the link graph
(edges weighted by |phi|). `n_core_loci` are claimed by every member and
`n_union_loci` by any. `mutual_best` is `r s$mutual_best`: when `FALSE`, a
program may link to several programs of another trait, because EBMF can split
one biological module into two programs within a trait; when `TRUE`, only
links where each program is the other's closest match are kept, so each
program has at most one partner per other trait.

```{r results = "asis"}
if (nrow(family_table) == 0) {
  cat("No program pairs were linked, so there are no families.\n\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
    "%d families from %d linked programs (%d programs have no link); modularity %.2f.\n\n",
    nrow(family_table), nrow(x$nodes), as.integer(x$n_unlinked), x$modularity
  ))
  cat('<div class="table-wrap">')
  print(knitr::kable(family_table, format = "html", escape = FALSE, caption = "Families"))
  cat("</div>")
}
```

```{r fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
if (nrow(family_table) > 0) print(gpmapr::plot_families(x))
```

## Do families recover the same biology?

Annotations play no part in forming a link. For each family, the
high-confidence SNPs of its programs in each trait are enriched separately,
against that trait's own SNPs, for trait categories and tissues, and for
Reactome and KEGG pathways through their colocalizing QTL genes. A family
whose traits independently surface the same category, tissue or pathway has
support beyond the loadings that created it. A SNP set holding most of its
trait's SNPs is compared against a background that is largely itself, so
"none" there is expected.

```{r results = "asis"}
if (is.null(x$family_enrichment)) {
  cat("This result was not annotated (`annotate = FALSE`).\n\n")
} else if (nrow(biology) == 0) {
  cat("No families to annotate.\n\n")
} else {
  shown <- biology[, c("family", "trait_name", "programs", "n_snps", "categories", "tissues", "reactome", "kegg")]
  cat('<div class="table-wrap">')
  print(knitr::kable(shown, format = "html", caption = "Enrichment of each family's SNPs, per trait"))
  cat("</div>")
}
```

## Reading the results

- **Profile first, loci second.** Two traits that share few fine-mapped loci
  can still share programs; their links are usually `too_few_loci`.
- **`too_few_loci` and `disagree` differ.** The first means the loci cannot
  check the profile match; the second that they were checked and the shared
  SNPs do not carry both programs.
- **Read `top_traits`.** Near-duplicate traits each count separately, so check
  the names, not just `n_eff_traits`.
- **The profile sign is a direction.** Each trait is oriented to its own risk
  allele, so antagonism mirrors the profile (phi < 0). A `direction_check` of
  `conflict` is worth inspecting.
- **Cutoffs are judgements.** The phi cutoffs follow factor-analysis
  conventions, not calibration on genetic loadings.
- **Sample overlap and winner's curse are not corrected.** Same-cohort traits
  bias `rg` away from zero, and shared loci are selected by both traits.
